scenes.text: Unreeled is an open-source app for Instagram. Here's how it keeps your account private.
You log in on Instagram's own page. Unreeled never reads or stores your password.
After that, your phone talks straight to Instagram. Nothing you see or send passes through a server of ours.
No analytics, no tracking, no ads. Unreeled collects nothing about you.
It downloads one thing: a short list that keeps it working, signed by the project so nobody else can change it.
Log out, and everything it saved on your phone is deleted.
Notifications are optional. They do pass through a server, Unreeled's relay, but it can't read them. Here's why.
Your phone makes a pair of keys, and the private key never leaves it. Instagram gets the public key and a push address, just as a browser would.
Instagram encrypts each notification for your phone. It travels through Mozilla's push service, Unreeled's relay, and Apple's. None of them has the key. Only your phone can read it.

The relay keeps a random ID, your phone's address at Apple, the push address, and when your phone was last seen. It sees when a notification passes, and its size. Never what it says, or whose account it is.
Turn notifications off, or log out, and the keys are deleted and the relay forgets your phone.
The app and the relay are open source, so anyone can check all of this.
One caution: Unreeled is unofficial, and Instagram could restrict an account that uses it. The details are at unreeled.app.
